overview: Model-based economic evaluation of lowering the heat-health activation threshold by 2 degrees, over five heat seasons, from the health system and health unit perspective.
population: Residents of the region in heat seasons 2027 to 2031.
exposure: Activation threshold lowered by 2 degrees compared with the current threshold.
procedures: Decision model combining activation days, the rate ratio for heat-related visits on alert days, and regional costs per activation day; probabilistic sensitivity analysis.

outcomes.name: Incremental net cost per heat-related emergency visit avoided
outcomes.measure: Difference in cost divided by difference in heat-related visits over five seasons

outcomes.name: Heat-related emergency visits among adults aged 65 and over
Cooling centre operating cost per activation day
outcomes.measure: Staff, venue and transport cost per day

outcomes.name: Activation days without excess heat morbidity
outcomes.measure: Days activated under the lower threshold with visits at or below the non-heat baseline

outcomes.name: Outreach calls completed
outcomes.measure: Calls completed to registered residents per activation day
outcomes.why: Delivery of the component that reaches those at risk.

feasibility: Depends on emergency department and ambulance cost data for 2023 to 2026, not yet available.
biasMitigation: Effect estimate varied across its interval

biasFlags.label: Borrowed effect estimate
biasFlags.note: The threshold effect interval includes no effect.

flags: A cost ratio as the primary outcome

summary: Economic evaluation protocol with a cost ratio as primary outcome; one outcome role is not a valid role.
